title: Finite Q3 local Gibbs/energy-weighted commutator-sum replacement audit
question: Can the raw finite-Q3 commutator-sum coefficient be replaced, on a named local common-core proxy, by two-sided Gibbs and energy-weighted pair seminorms that remain controlled across the declared cutoff, beta, volume, and shifted source supports?

named_proxy.core: finite Schwartz/oscillator matrix proxy on each overlapping union U of Q3 term supports
named_proxy.state: rho_U=exp(-beta H_U)/Tr(exp(-beta H_U)) for the induced Q3 Hamiltonian on U
named_proxy.energy: K_U=I+H_U-min(spec(H_U)) I, shifted positive before K_U^(1/2)
named_proxy.energy_weighted_pair_seminorm: sqrt(sum of Frobenius squares of K_U^(1/2) X rho_U^(1/2), K_U^(1/2) X* rho_U^(1/2), X K_U^(1/2) rho_U^(1/2), X* K_U^(1/2) rho_U^(1/2))
named_proxy.pair_operator: X=[H_j,H_k] for every overlapping onsite/bond pair; disjoint pairs are omitted by exact tensor locality
named_proxy.coefficient: sum of pair seminorms, with all-pair and source-touching aggregates reported separately

adversarial_review.check: rho_U is explicitly the normalized Gibbs matrix of the induced union Hamiltonian; it is not identified with a restriction of an infinite-volume KMS state or with a product state.
The four energy-weighted legs are constructed separately, so no commutation of K_U with X or rho_U is assumed.
Only overlapping onsite/bond supports are evaluated; a reference full-tensor embedding is compared at the registered volume/cutoff.
Every declared cutoff and beta rebuilds oscillator matrices, local Hamiltonians, Gibbs factors and weights; finite grid ratios are not asymptotic bounds.
Source-touching aggregates use the explicit support lists for each graph volume; no unlisted translation or arbitrary-shape claim is made.
The weighted sums are labelled candidate proxies; the raw operator-norm Lie-Trotter inequality is not reused with a seminorm lacking a proved submultiplicative defect estimate.
No common unbounded domain, thermodynamic history, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure is inferred.

lean_crosscheck.role: R334 checks exact rational seminorm and coefficient bookkeeping plus the scope firewall; matrix exponentials, spectral factors, local Gibbs restrictions, cutoff asymptotics and QFT limits remain Python/open analysis.

qft_interface.closed: A reproducible finite local-union table for raw, Gibbs two-sided and K^(1/2)-Gibbs four-leg commutator-sum candidates across the declared cutoff, beta, volume and source-support grid.
qft_interface.open: A global-state-compatible common-core estimate, cutoff/volume/beta-uniform weighted coefficient, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, thermodynamic history, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference or Sector-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Use the finite comparison only to select the analytic route: if the local weighted coefficient grows, retain a route-local stress boundary and seek cancellation-aware D,delta-D estimates; if it is stable, prove a global-state/common-core transfer and exhaustion estimate before any common-alpha promotion.
no_overclaim: This is a finite local-state proxy audit. It does not prove a global KMS state, a common unbounded core, a thermodynamic QFT dynamics, a mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite local Gibbs and energy-weighted commutator-sum diagnostic only.
